evidence:
Nandini has dated photographs of her 2019 market stall showing the logo on the banner, and 2020 invoices from a local printer for logo-printed labels. She has Instagram posts from 2020 onward showing the packaging, and online order records from 2021 with sales figures. Her total sales are modest, mostly within one region, and some early invoices are handwritten without the business name. A customer testimonial from 2020 mentions the logo by description but not by image.

The company's registration certificate is dated 2024, covers "spices and condiments," and its mark is a stylized pot without a leaf in red and gold. Its notice includes side-by-side images but also a claim of "pan-national reputation" with no supporting documents. A search of the trademark register shows no earlier filings by Nandini and no other similar marks in the same class. There is no evidence of actual confusion, no complaints or misdirected orders, and the company's sales are mainly through large retail chains that Nandini does not use.

User statement (unverified): She also says the two logos are similar only in the use of a pot, while hers has a leaf and a different color scheme, and that her customers have never confused the two brands.

events.description: Nandini Rao runs "Kaveri Kitchen," a small home-based packaged-spice business that began selling at local markets in 2019 and moved to online sales in 2021.
She used a distinctive logo, a stylized copper pot with a leaf, on her packaging, social media, and market stall banners.
She never registered the trademark because she believed her business was too small to need it.
In March this year, she received a legal notice from "Kaveri Foods Pvt.
Ltd.," a larger company, claiming that her use of the logo infringes its registered trademark, which was filed in 2024.
The notice demands that she stop using the logo, destroy her packaging, and pay a penalty.
Nandini says she used the logo years before the company even applied.
She also says the two logos are similar only in the use of a pot, while hers has a leaf and a different color scheme, and that her customers have never confused the two brands.
The company's notice gives her 15 days to comply.
She is frightened about losing her packaging stock, which she has just reordered in bulk.
She wants to know whether prior use gives her any rights, whether she can challenge the company's registration, whether she should rebrand, and how to respond to the notice.

suggestions.title: Original records and an evidence log
suggestions.look_for: Keep records you lawfully have, with their surrounding context. For each item note the related event, who provided it, when you received it, and any transfer.
suggestions.why: The log distinguishes what you observed from what someone later told you and makes it easier to check the source.
suggestions.action: Keep an unchanged original and label working copies. Avoid editing originals, guessing gaps, or sharing evidence publicly.
